notes: The core idea is missing. The car is already glossy teal in frame 1, so there is no salt-grey winter 'before' state and no transformation. Open on a dull, salt-crusted, grey-filmed car rolling into a dark bay. Then hold the same car, same angle, at the reveal, so the payoff reads as before and after.

Frame 1 is incoherent: a wheel hangs upside down at top left and the space is confusing. Replace it with a clean establishing shot of the car entering the bay with headlights cutting through the dark.
Frame 3, the foam close-up, shows garbled letter-like artifacts on the hood ('BAUL…'). That is a clear AI tell; regenerate it as clean foam texture with no glyphs.

Frames 7-8 are a chaotic crown splash on the hood, not water beading off ceramic coating. The brief asks for tight macro beads rolling off a hydrophobic surface. That shot sells the product; the explosion does not.
The polisher shot should show swirls disappearing in one pass: a split surface, hazy behind and mirror ahead. The current frame is just a hand on a polisher.
The steam/interior shot (frame 6) has steam aimed at the exterior from an interior POV, which is spatially confusing. Either commit to a clean interior deep-clean beat or cut it.
The light-bar reflection beat (frames 9-11) is the strongest material. Linger on a crisp, undistorted hexagon or light-bar reflection in the hood as the hero frame.
The ending inverts the brief. The detailer walks toward the camera, posing, instead of stepping back to admire the car. Restage it: he steps back into frame edge and the car is the hero.

The end-card text sits over a busy, foggy image, so 'Your car. Like the first day.' is low-contrast and small. Either darken or blur the plate or go straight to the black card. Also, the concept label appears both in the card body and as the corner label; keep only the corner label.

The look is crushed orange/teal with heavy haze on every frame, which feels generic and stock. Vary the lighting: start cold and grey, end crisp and clean-white, so the grade itself tells the salt-to-mirror story.
Check that no badges or logos appear on the car; the grille emblem area in frame 11 should be clearly blank.
